title: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP: semantic index to shorten agent tool-call sequences
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned semantic-index enhancement from the documented ERP MCP server. The roadmap supports its dates and automatic enablement, and Microsoft Learn supports the client allowlist path, preview CLI command and billing qualifications.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a semantic index of available ERP menu items, entities and actions.
claims.quote: a semantic index of the available menu items, entities, and actions

claims.claim: The enhancement provides a single point of entry for MCP tools.
claims.quote: with a single point of entry for MCP tools

claims.claim: The planned enhancement optimises tool execution sequences instead of relying on orchestration that can choose unnecessarily long sequences.
claims.quote: The orchestration can select the tool execution sequence and can include more tool calls than are required.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes a performance enhancement without stating a change to security-role filtering or data boundaries.
claims.quote: This enhancement to the MCP server improves performance and accuracy of the server response by enabling the server to use optimal tool execution sequences

claims.claim: The roadmap does not say whether the enhancement changes billing.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server now uses a semantic index of target ERP menu items, entities, and actions to improve performance and accuracy of tool calls by optimizing the sequence of tool executions for agentic operations.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not name finance and operations end users outside agents as an affected audience.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: The Dynamics 365 ERP Model Context Protocol server lets agents work with finance and operations data and business logic.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server provides a dynamic framework for agents to perform data operations and access the business logic of finance and operations apps.

claims.claim: The documented dynamic server has data, form and action tool categories.
claims.quote: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server provides three categories of tools for working with the data and business logic of finance and operations apps: ... Data tools ... Form tools ... Action tools

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The documented form_find_menu_item tool finds menu items.
claims.quote: | `form_find_menu_item` | Find a menu item |

claims.claim: The documented data_find_entity_type tool finds entity types.
claims.quote: Find OData entity types. This tool is needed for calling the `data_get_entity_metadata` tool.

claims.claim: The roadmap's more-info page describes the separate ERP Analytics MCP server for Business performance analytics.
claims.quote: The ERP Analytics MCP server works alongside the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server to enable powerful agent workflows that combine analytical insights with transactional actions:

claims.claim: The ERP Analytics MCP feature is documented as preview.
claims.quote: This feature is a preview feature. It's subject to the preview supplemental terms of use.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the roadmap's semantic-index and single-entry-point enhancement.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index optimal tool execution single entry point enable feature management version. Opened copilot-mcp and erp-analytics-mcp-overview; results describe current tools and distinct Work IQ indexing, not this enhancement.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No switch specific to the semantic index is documented, and the client allowlist is not documented as such a switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index optimal tool execution single entry point enable feature management version; Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index security data storage switch configuration. Opened copilot-mcp, mcp-security and mcp-foundry; only server-wide enablement and client controls.

claims.claim: The documentation does not describe whether the planned semantic index stores anything.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index security data storage switch configuration. Opened mcp-security and copilot-mcp; neither describes the planned index's storage. Work IQ search results concern a different semantic indexing capability.

claims.claim: A finance and operations version requirement specific to this enhancement is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index optimal tool execution single entry point enable feature management version. Opened copilot-mcp; read version 10.0.49 release-note search excerpts. No result specified a version for the semantic-index enhancement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No rate or price specific to the semantic-index enhancement is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 ERP MCP semantic index pricing licensing Copilot Credits tool execution. Opened copilot-mcp Licensing; read returned licensing excerpts. Published rates cover ERP MCP tool calls generally, with no separate semantic-index rate.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The current server returns only menu items accessible to the authenticated user's security role.
claims.quote: when the agent calls the `form_find_menu_item` tool, it returns only menu items to which that security role has access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The current server filters returned entities to objects accessible to the user context's security role.
claims.quote: the entities returned in the response to the `data_find_entity_type` tool and APIs returned in the response to the `api_find_actions` tool only include objects to which the security role for the user context has access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The current server filters returned actions to those accessible to the user's security role.
claims.quote: When the view model for a form is returned to the agent, it includes only data, fields, and actions to which the user role has access.

claims.claim: The server rejects explicit calls to actions or objects outside the user's role.
claims.quote: The system rejects any explicit calls to actions or objects to which the user role doesn't have access.

claims.claim: The documented MCP server does not store customer data.
claims.quote: It returns results to the calling client for the duration of the request, but doesn't store customer data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Operations run under the authenticated identity and its finance and operations security context.
claims.quote: Operations run under the authenticated user's identity and security context in finance and operations apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Finance and operations security enforces authorisation, and its existing roles, duties and privileges govern what an MCP agent can reach.
claims.quote: If administrators want to change what a user can access or modify through the MCP server, they should update the same security roles, duties, privileges, and policies that they use for other finance and operations channels.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Allowed MCP clients configuration controls which agent platforms can connect to the server in an environment.
claims.quote: Administrators can also control which agent clients are allowed to connect to the MCP server. When you enable the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server in your environment, choose which agent platforms can access the server.

claims.claim: ERP MCP data tools support create, update and delete operations, so the operations whose sequences are being optimised include writes.
claims.quote: Data tools: These tools enable the agent to perform standard data operations to create, read, update, and delete data in your finance and operations apps environment.

claims.claim: ERP MCP form tools include an operation to save forms.
claims.quote: | `form_save_form` | Saves form |

claims.claim: Microsoft does not guarantee support assistance for errors when the server is added to the Copilot for finance and operations apps agent.
claims.quote: Although you're not blocked from adding the MCP server to the agent, you might experience errors in the execution. Microsoft support doesn't guarantee assistance for resolving errors or problems for these scenarios.

claims.claim: ERP MCP agent use has agent-orchestration and MCP-server-execution cost components.
claims.quote: When you use the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server in an agent, you incur two types of costs: 1. The agent orchestration cost (LLM cost), and 2. The MCP server execution cost (tool calls to the server).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: In Copilot Studio, MCP tool calls are billed as Agent Action at a fixed rate per tool call.
claims.quote: When you use the MCP server in Copilot Studio, the tool calls align with the Agent Action feature, which bills at a fixed rate per tool call.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio Agent Action rate covers orchestration and MCP-server execution.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, billing for the Agent Action feature includes both the LLM cost for orchestration and the execution of the MCP server.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio adds no incremental MCP-server execution charge.
claims.quote: There's no incremental charge for the execution cost of the MCP server.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The standard execution rate for agents on clients other than Copilot Studio is 0.1 Copilot Credits per ERP MCP tool call.
claims.quote: For agents built on other agent clients, usage of the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server incurs a cost of one copilot credit per 10 tool calls to the server (or 0.1 credits per tool call).

claims.claim: Other agent clients separately bill orchestration at their own token-consumption rates.
claims.quote: The cost for the LLM orchestration is a separate charge by the agent client for token consumption, based on the rates of that client.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dynamics 365 Finance Premium users are exempt from tool-execution billing on clients other than Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: The following premium licenses are exempt from the tool execution billing for agents built on clients other than Copilot Studio. ... Dynamics 365 Finance Premium

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Premium users are exempt from tool-execution billing on clients other than Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: The following premium licenses are exempt from the tool execution billing for agents built on clients other than Copilot Studio. ... Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Premium

claims.claim: The ERP MCP page says Copilot Studio agent usage is included in the Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: For Copilot Studio agents, agent usage is included in the Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: Copilot USL users' Copilot Studio agent calls under their authenticated identity incur no additional ERP MCP credit consumption.
claims.quote: Business to Employee usage of Copilot Studio agents ... the agent operates by using the authenticated Copilot USL user's identity. In these cases, the tool calls to the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server don't incur additional credit consumption.

claims.claim: The documented ERP MCP prerequisites specify at least version 10.0.47, 10.0.46 PQU-2 or 10.0.45 PQU-7.
claims.quote: The product version of Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps must be at least: - 10.0.47 - 10.0.46 PQU-2 - 10.0.45 PQU-7

claims.claim: ERP MCP requires a Tier 2 or above environment or a Unified Developer Environment.
claims.quote: Your environment is Tier 2 or above, or a Unified Developer Environment.

claims.claim: ERP MCP is not supported on Cloud Hosted Environments.
claims.quote: The MCP server isn't supported on Cloud Hosted Environments (CHE).

claims.claim: The existing ERP MCP server is enabled by default.
claims.quote: The MCP server is enabled by default.

claims.claim: The existing Dynamics 365 ERP Model Context Protocol server feature is managed in Feature management, as a server-wide prerequisite.
claims.quote: Enable the Dynamics 365 ERP Model Context Protocol server feature in Feature Management if not already enabled.

claims.claim: In the finance and operations apps client, System administration > Setup > Allowed MCP clients > New > Allowed reaches the client allow control.
claims.quote: Go to System administration > Setup > Allowed MCP clients to open the Allowed MCP clients page. ... Select New on the action ribbon. ... Allowed | true

claims.claim: dataverse mcp allow <appId> --erp allows the application on the linked Finance and Operations instance.
claims.quote: dataverse mcp allow <appId> [options] ... --erp | Allow the application on the linked Finance and Operations instance instead of Dataverse.

claims.claim: The Dataverse CLI is preview.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The allow command uses the current profile's environment, with --erp selecting its linked Finance and Operations instance.
claims.quote: Ensure that a Microsoft Entra application is in the Dataverse MCP allowed clients list for the current profile's environment. ... --erp | Allow the application on the linked Finance and Operations instance instead of Dataverse.

claims.claim: The appId argument is an application client ID GUID.
claims.quote: The `<appId>` argument is the application (client) ID to allow, as a GUID.

claims.claim: The authenticated user running the command needs Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.
claims.quote: The authenticated user must have Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.

claims.claim: A new Allowed MCP clients record supplies a Name.
claims.quote: | Name | Provide a name for your MCP connection |

claims.claim: A new Allowed MCP clients record supplies the application client ID in ClientId.
claims.quote: | ClientId | The Application (client) ID value of your new registered app from the Entra ID app registration |

claims.claim: The new client record sets Allowed to true.
claims.quote: | Allowed | `true` |

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects published ERP MCP metering alongside licence-based exemptions and inclusion.
claims.quote: Tool execution cost ... Billed at 0.1 Copilot Credits per tool call ... The following premium licenses are exempt from the tool execution billing for agents built on clients other than Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects the documented per-tool-call Copilot Credits meter, whose charge varies with billable call count.
claims.quote: For agents built on other agent clients, usage of the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server incurs a cost of one copilot credit per 10 tool calls to the server (or 0.1 credits per tool call).
